definition: Artificial intelligence rhetoric (AI rhetoric) is a term primarily applied to persuasive text and speech generated by chatbots using generative artificial intelligence, although the term can also apply to the language that humans type or speak when communicating with a chatbot.
details: This emerging field of rhetoric scholarship is related to the fields of digital rhetoric and human-computer interaction.

explainer.lead: Artificial intelligence rhetoric examines the persuasive language on both sides of a chatbot conversation: what people say to the system and what it says back. It matters because these exchanges do more than transfer information; they can frame choices, make appeals, and influence responses.

tiers.eli5: Imagine talking with a very quick writer who can answer almost any message. AI rhetoric looks at how you word your request and how the writer words its answer to sound convincing. It is a bit like studying both sides of a debate, even when one side is a computer program.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encounter AI rhetoric when designing or evaluating chatbot conversations and other generative-AI interfaces. Review prompts together with generated text or speech, since human messages are part of the phenomenon too. A useful pitfall to avoid is judging an output only for factual correctness while overlooking how its wording, framing, and appeals persuade the reader or listener.
tiers.paperLevel: AI rhetoric = {persuasive text or speech generated by chatbots using generative AI} ∪ {language typed or spoken by humans when communicating with chatbots}. It is an emerging area of rhetoric scholarship related to digital rhetoric and human-computer interaction. Its scope therefore includes rhetorical activity on both sides of the exchange, rather than denoting a model architecture or an evaluation metric.

explainer.example: A user asks a chatbot, “Give me three convincing reasons to cycle to work,” and the chatbot replies with an appeal to saving money, improving health, and avoiding traffic. AI rhetoric covers both the user’s request for a persuasive answer and the appeals made in the generated text.

usedIn.name: Chatbot conversations
usedIn.detail: Examines both users’ messages and the persuasive language generated in reply.

usedIn.name: Generative AI communication
usedIn.detail: Studies persuasive text and speech produced through interactions with chatbots.

usedIn.name: Digital rhetoric
usedIn.detail: Provides a related scholarly field for studying communication in digital settings.

usedIn.name: Human-computer interaction
usedIn.detail: Offers a related field for examining language exchanged between people and chatbots.

explainer.intuition: A chatbot exchange is not just a question followed by an answer: both sides use language that can guide, frame, and persuade. AI rhetoric gives scholars a way to study that language across the whole exchange.
howItWorks: A person types or speaks a message to a chatbot.
The person’s wording forms part of the human side of AI rhetoric.
The chatbot uses generative AI to produce text or speech.
Persuasive features of that output form the generated side of AI rhetoric.
Scholars examine the exchange in relation to digital rhetoric and human-computer interaction.
explainer.whyItMatters: The concept draws attention to persuasion throughout human–chatbot communication, not merely to whether an answer is accurate. Studying both human and generated language can clarify how requests shape replies and how replies address their audiences.
misconceptions: It is not limited to language produced by chatbots; human messages to chatbots can also count.
It is not a name for generative AI itself, but for a rhetorical focus on language in chatbot communication.
It is not restricted to written exchanges, because generated speech and spoken human language can also be included.
